html:
Uzeyir Hajibeyov was a composer, born in 1885 and raised in Shusha, whose opera Leyli and Majnun, staged in Baku in 1908, was the first opera in the Muslim world.

He set the old love story, told in verse by Fuzuli, to mugham singing with a Western orchestra. His musical comedy Arshin Mal Alan, of 1913, was filmed several times and became popular across the Middle East. He founded a conservatory in Baku and wrote the music of the national anthem of the Azerbaijan Democratic Republic in 1919, which was taken up again in 1992. His opera Koroghlu, of 1937, became a classic of Soviet Azerbaijan. His birthday is Music Day in Azerbaijan.
